c: Pentagram summons a purple glyph with golden lining, visual details of which increase as Pentagram levels up. After summoning, the glyph shatters, instantly erasing every enemy, their drops, and all items on the screen, except for stage items. Pentagram always deals damage equal to the max health of the enemy. If it is lower than 660, the damage number is overwritten to display it between 655 and 665.

Aside from the visibility of items, one way the player can observe if the Pentagram erased items or not, for each time it is activated, is if they have "Damage Numbers" enabled in the Options. An indication of damage numbers through enemies means the Pentagram did not erase items, while no indication of damage numbers means it erased the items.
Pentagram's symbol gets progressively more complex as its level increases:
At Level 1, the golden linings are an

in the middle within a hexagram symbol having some missing lines from being two completed ones, a ring of small symbols, and three concentric rings on top of a purple circle. The inner ring is in the purple circle and close to its perimeter, and the outer ones are very similar in size, they are bigger than the purple circle. The smallest and the middle ring have a straight line connecting them at 12 points, similar to a clock.
At Level 4, another golden ring is added and connects to the points at the hexagram, the symbols are much bigger and clearly form words instead of being evenly spaced.

At Level 5, the hexagram is replaced with a triangle with circles at the tips, each circle has a symbol in it. The triangle is partially covering another two rings with more symbols between them, also clearly forming words.

At Level 7, two concentric hexagons are added to encompass the inner set of rings and symbols and touch the outer set. The lines connecting the outermost two rings in the cardinal direction are replaced with two lines spreading out from the outer ring, similar to a compass with arrows pointing out.

At Level 8, the triangle with circle tips is replaced by three concentric hexagons, which are rotated by 30 degrees from the original two. The smallest one is similar in size to the middle one. The biggest hexagon and the middle hexagon have lines connecting between the vertices. Between those two hexagons, each of the six sections has symbols, seemingly replaced and fused with the inner set of circles and symbols. The biggest hexagon's vertices touch the only set of circles and symbols left.
Depending on its level and the
stat, there is a chance for a blue symbol to appear instead, which only erases enemies and not the drops and items, similar to the effect of the Rosary. Pentagram can be affected by
, but there is a hard-coded limit of 15 seconds on how often Pentagram can trigger.
To reach Pentagram's 15-second Cooldown limit, a Cooldown bonus of:
-83.33% is required at level 1
-81.25% is required at level 2
-78.57% is required at level 4
-76.92% is required at level 6
-75% is required at level 8
Some enemies are completely unaffected by Pentagram.

before minute 30. However, they do not drop chests from the blast even if it does not erase any items.
Pentagram initially has a 10% chance to not destroy items, which is increased at levels 3, 5 and 7. This chance is affected by the character's
For general purposes, the total chance to not erase items can be calculated as:
chanceWithLuck=chance⋅totalLuck
In more detail, the
for the Pentagram is handled via the following procedure:
First, a random number x is generated from the
: x ~ U[0,1]. This is rounded to 2 decimal places.
Next, x is scaled down by the character's total
to become x/totalLuck.
Lastly, the result is compared with the current Pentagram activation threshold, and triggers item destruction if x/totalLuck > Threshold.
For example, assume a level 5 Pentagram, with x = 0.5. This leads to a threshold of 0.45.
With +0% Luck (=100% total Luck), 0.5/1 = 0.5 is greater than 0.45, hence item destruction is triggered.
With +60% Luck (=160% total Luck), 0.5/1.6 = 0.31 is less than 0.45, hence item destruction is not triggered.
With enough Luck, it is possible to ensure that items will not be destroyed even with the max roll of x = 1:
At level 1, the threshold is 10%, +900% Luck is required (=1000% total Luck) as beyond 1/10 is always less than 0.1.
At level 3, the threshold is 25%, +300% Luck is required (=400% total Luck) as beyond 1/4 is always less than 0.25.
At level 5, the threshold is 45%, +123% Luck is required (=223% total Luck) as beyond 1/2.2 is always less than 0.45.
At level 7, the threshold is 65%, +54% Luck is required (=154% total Luck) as beyond 1.538461 is less less than 0.65.

Since Pentagram has the ability to destroy Pickups and Treasure Chests, it is inadvisable to select it too early to evolve it into Gorgeous Moon. Even with
making up for the experience loss, Treasure Chests are not easily replaceable.

Destroying Pickups could be beneficial in niche circumstances, for example, in no movement challenges once there are enough experience gems built up, a red one that consolidates extra experience will form, and the character with limited
cannot collect any more gems to level up. After a purple Pentagram is summoned, enemy kills can generate experience gems to be collected again.
Upgrading
while Pentagram is in lower levels is inadvisable, as it would trigger the Pentagram a bit more frequently, thus making the destruction of items statistically a bit more frequent.
should be avoided as well, at least while the Pentagram is still in the lower levels, as pickups and Treasure Chests risk being destroyed too.

If the player is near or surrounded by the items gathered by the Mad Groove and they are in the Level Up screen, the player should avoid leveling up the Pentagram if it is an option, especially if it is in a lower level. Doing so would trigger the Pentagram immediately after leveling it up and likely cause the destruction of items, especially at lower levels.

Even though Pentagram erases Treasure Chests, if a boss that would have dropped one is erased, the Treasure Chest is then dropped by a different enemy. However, if the boss has no guarantee of dropping a chest, there is still a chance of receiving nothing.

You can mitigate the loss of items from this weapon by timing the activation, if you have not had the circle pop for a while or using a table with Cooldown accurately calculated, move elsewhere and keep your gems and chest off-screen, wait for the Pentagram to trigger and then move back in to collect the stuff you wanted before. With a little bit of luck, you will get to keep the gems from the enemies you screen wipe as well.
Because some enemies like The Reaper or bosses at the 25th minute (in some stages) are immune to Pentagram's instant kill effect, it cannot be relied on as your only tool for killing enemies.

Pentagram is a great weapon to take near the end of a run when you already have 4 or 5 good weapons and you do not need anything else. Since you do not need more experience, its main downside is meaningless.

As with other weapons, taking or upgrading Pentagram, either from leveling up or upgrading it from a Treasure Chest - will instantly activate it. This can be used to your advantage, as it allows you to clear multiple screens in succession in the late game, or to save yourself from a pinch. However, be mindful that picking it with bad timing may destroy your valuables.
The Pentagram can be quite helpful in severely damaging or even entirely wiping off enemies that surround a

There was an update which was supposed to increase the base chance from 5% to 10%. However, due to an oversight, it remained at 5% as it was hardcoded. The increases stayed at 20%, 40% and 60% because upgrading adds a fixed value to the total instead of being hardcoded as the wording may suggest. It was fixed in update 0.3.1.
With the update that
comes with, the max level of Pentagram is increased by one from seven to eight. However, the new level simply splits the original level 6 effect of reducing
by 10 s to 5 at levels 6 and 8.
Compared to other weapons that still have only 7 levels like
and

, Pentagram originally might not have had an evolution planned for it, but maybe it was deemed not powerful enough with its downsides. Later, Laurel and Clock Lancet are given unique evolutions using new passive items from
, further divorcing the original trio.

In patch 0.8.0, Limit Breaking Pentagram to have a 100% chance of saving items and getting one more level up afterwards, will hardlock the game and require the player to close the game to restart. This has been patched in a follow-up patch a few days later.

If the player has reached the 100% chance of saving items since the small patch, every level up prompts the Gold Bag or Floor Chicken choice, despite the player choosing the "always" options to not hardlock the game. There is no remedy if you have limited yourself to one weapon only and did not get
to evolve it into Gorgeous Moon. It is eventually fixed.
If the player has Pentagram available, then collects a Gold Finger, Pentagram will be used the moment Gold Finger's effect begins, regardless of the cooldown of Pentagram.
